info.title: Cost per gigabyte
info.text: Hard disk storage costs a few pence per gigabyte; SSD storage costs several times more, although the gap keeps narrowing.

info.title: Speed in numbers
info.text: A hard disk transfers roughly 100-200 MB per second; a modern NVMe SSD can exceed 5,000 MB per second.

info.title: Helium drives
info.text: Some large hard disks are filled with helium instead of air, so the platters meet less resistance and more can be packed in.

info.title: Rewritable discs
info.text: CD-R and DVD-R can be written once; RW versions use a material that can be melted back and rewritten hundreds of times.

info.title: Tape robots
info.text: Data centres use robot arms to fetch tapes from racks, like a huge automated library.

info.title: Right tool, right job
info.text: Big systems use all three: SSDs for speed, hard disks for bulk, and tape for archives.
